industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the sector rows carrying the view. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): technology saw $5.5 billion of net selling in the week, the most since January 2025 (Jefferies, 17 Oct), the rotation came out of it, and Wood says 'the easy money in semis is made'; against that, Jefferies finds sector pockets still upgrading inside it (analogue chips, optical networking, artificial-intelligence memory) and Morgan Stanley still rates North American semiconductors Attractive. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: B now, B prior at industry level, carried by Semiconductors at A. The industry row stays C because the industry is split: Semiconductors (D), Software B2B Enterprise (D), Fintech (D) and Games (D) carry the Underweight; IT services, Hardware and vertical software stay Neutral. Counter-case for D: the heaviest net selling in 21 months is a regime statement; for B: the only industry with upgrades inside the sell-off.

sector.why: Underweight, carried unchanged, with the sector now split by the sources. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): artificial-intelligence-linked semiconductors fell eight straight sessions to 16 Oct, technology net selling was the heaviest since January 2025, Wood says 'the easy money in semis is made', Korea fell about 20% in October on de-grossing, and the AI credits that set this row (the neoclouds) are 'the epicentre of the funding cost debate' (Goldman, 19 Oct); against it, Jefferies (22 Oct) is 'incrementally positive' on analogue chips with a read-across to Infineon and STMicroelectronics, sees China's equipment imports up 26% as the upside for 2027-28, and Morgan Stanley still rates North American semiconductors Attractive, while on equipment Jefferies' own headline is 'ASML - Still not excited'. Neither condition for C is met (no stabilisation read on the AI credits; no sell-side buy call on the European sector). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: A now, A prior, the disagreement stated: the market still ranks the sector first while cutting its multiple. Ten of the 149 Pool stocks. Counter-case: the analogue upcycle 'has more legs' into 2027, demand was never the problem, and a D on ten Pool names pushes the Lists away from the one European industry with upgrades; the analogue read is a reason to look at STMicroelectronics stock by stock, not to move a row that is mostly equipment.

geography.why: Overweight, carried unchanged. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the Swiss index is among those Goldman (19 Oct) names as rallying alongside non-AI and low-beta exposures, which is the rotation this row was set on; the Swiss National Bank was not re-read this week, so last week's 'not hiking' stands. Relative strength is not graded by country. Counter-case unchanged: the franc takes 2 to 3 points a year off a Swiss exporter's reported profit (Sonova memo), and five of the Swiss Pool names are semiconductor names inside an Underweight sector. Back to C if the SNB joins the hikers or the franc reverses.

memo.verdict: PROGRESS to Early-Stage Assessment. Medium conviction. Direction stated explicitly in the memo: bullish on the franchise, neutral on the security, outright bearish on the entry point at 41.3x forward earnings. Condition attached: the Early-Stage Assessment must open with Elements E2 and E3 so the total-shareholder-return arithmetic gates the qualitative work rather than following it; if that arithmetic fails from CHF 645.4 the case parks there. The memo recommends progression while the risks family on the same disk recommends PARK for twelve months. The memo addresses that disagreement by name in Section E across five reconciliation points and adopts the risks family's valuation concern in full while rejecting its stage verdict.
case: The memo's argument runs in this order.

First, the change forces are exceptional and, unusually, realised rather than forecast. Second-quarter 2026 order intake reached CHF 500m, up 102% year on year, at a 1.7x book-to-bill, following CHF 356.3m in the first quarter at 1.6x. The 2027 net sales target of CHF 1.5bn to CHF 1.7bn was placed under formal upward review in July 2026. That combination is what earns E1.RA1 its [A]: no peer in the six-name set printed a 102% year-on-year order increase in the same quarter, and none carried a formal upward revision of a medium-term revenue target in the same quarter.

The external change force is technological rather than merely cyclical, which is why content growth is largely independent of unit volumes. Gate-All-Around at sub-2nm raises vacuum process steps by over 25%, triples atomic layer deposition steps and raises epitaxy steps sixfold. Jefferies models etch and deposition layers expanding 36%, from 44 to 60 layers, at 2nm. Advanced nodes require 2,200 process steps, a 193% increase over legacy 28nm. High numerical-aperture extreme ultraviolet doubles internal vacuum exposure at about USD 300,000 of valve content per scanner. Wafer fab equipment forecasts for 2026 moved from USD 130bn to USD 145bn, a 23% expansion, with 2027 projected at USD 180bn across 140 new fabs; SEMI upgraded front-end process equipment to USD 152.20bn on 3 June 2026. Hyperscaler 2026 data-centre capital expenditure was set beyond USD 750bn, up 68%. The core vacuum valve market is projected at CHF 1.3bn to CHF 1.4bn by 2029 on a 12% compound rate, with vacuum equipment outpacing total wafer fab equipment by four points a year.
counter_case: Direction: bearish. Quantified endpoint CHF 275 to CHF 335 against a live price of CHF 645.4.

The risks family's own recommendation, quoted in the memo: park VAT Group shares for the next twelve months until multiple contraction provides a more attractive entry point. The memo adopts that valuation concern in full and rejects only the stage verdict.
triggers: - Evidence that would refute the memo's thesis: a single quarter of orders below CHF 300m, or a book-to-bill below 1.0x, would invalidate the big demand change-driven earnings upgrade setup that Element E8 identified as the primary fit.
- Third-quarter 2026 revenue against the guided CHF 355m to CHF 385m range, reported November 2026. This is the memo's named single decisive number.
- Second-half 2026 EBITDA margin: does it clear 31%, and what is the run-rate margin once the 709 hires are productive against the 33.5% full-year midpoint.
- Fourth-quarter 2026 book-to-bill as the cleanest available false-friend discriminator, measured against consignment inventory at major Western and Asian original equipment manufacturers.
- What total shareholder return is available from CHF 645.4 on Jefferies' FY27 earnings per share of CHF 12.29 at a 25x trough multiple versus a 40x base multiple.
- Realistic downside if the MATCH Act reaches subsystems, given direct Chinese sales at 28% of first-half 2026 revenue and total China exposure of 40% to 45%.
